title: The Heawood family is not the complete list of excluded minors for Colin de Verdière invariant at most 5
abstract:
We show that two intrinsically knotted graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ with 23 edges, on 11 and 12 vertices, have Colin de Verdière invariant $\mu=6$ and no minor in the Heawood family, the 78 graphs obtained from $K_7$ and $K_{3,3,1,1}$ by $\Delta Y$- and $Y\Delta$-transformations. So the Heawood family is not the complete list of excluded minors for $\mu\le5$, as van der Holst proposed; Mattman and Pavelescu stated this proposal as a conjecture and derived from it that $G_1$ and $G_2$ have $\mu=5$. More precisely, either the common minor $H$ of $G_1$ and $G_2$, a 4-regular graph with 11 vertices and 22 edges, is an excluded minor for $\mu\le5$, or $G_1$ and $G_2$ both are. It follows that the following two conjectures of van der Holst cannot both hold: (a) a graph is 4-flat if and only if $\mu\le5$; (b) the Heawood family is the complete list of excluded minors for 4-flat graphs. The lower bound $\mu\ge6$ is proved by explicit matrices certified in interval and exact rational arithmetic, and the minor exclusion by exhaustive enumeration. title: The Heawood family is not the complete list of excluded minors for 4-flat graphs
abstract:
A graph is 4-flat if the complex obtained by filling every simple cycle with a separate disk embeds piecewise linearly in four-dimensional space. The Heawood family consists of 78 graphs obtained from $K_7$ and $K_{3,3,1,1}$ by triangle–star and star–triangle transformations. Van der Holst proved that these graphs are not 4-flat; Georgakopoulos and Winter completed the proof that all 78 are excluded minors and conjectured that there are no other excluded minors for 4-flatness. We show that the known eleven-vertex, twenty-two-edge graph $H$ is not 4-flat and has no Heawood-family minor, resolving the completeness question negatively. Mattman and Pierce found by computer search that every proper minor of $H$ is 2-apex; this implies that $H$ itself is a further excluded minor. Mattman and Pierce found $H$, subsequently studied by Kim and Mattman. An earlier paper by the author proved that its one-edge extension $G_1$ has Colin de Verdière invariant 6 and no Heawood-family minor. This made 4-flatness completeness incompatible with van der Holst's proposed equivalence between 4-flatness and invariant at most 5. The new step is an explicit mod-two deleted-product cycle with invariant one. Van der Holst and Pendavingh's obstruction theorem therefore excludes an even map, and hence an embedding, of a cycle subcomplex of $H$ into four-dimensional space. Two separately written exact implementations evaluate the certificate, using moment-curve intersections and the recursive cellular invariant, respectively. title: No post-Lie algebra structures on pairs of perfect and nilpotent Lie algebras
abstract:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{n}$ be finite-dimensional Lie algebras on the same vector space over a field of characteristic zero, with $\mathfrak{n}$ nilpotent. We prove that if the pair $(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{n})$ carries a post-Lie algebra structure all of whose right multiplications have trace zero, then $\mathfrak{g}$ is solvable. Hence no nonzero perfect Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ admits a post-Lie algebra structure on $(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{n})$ with $\mathfrak{n}$ nilpotent. This answers a question of Burde and Dekimpe in the negative and proves the nilpotent case of a conjecture of Burde, Dekimpe and Monadjem. Nonexistence was known for abelian $\mathfrak{n}$, by a theorem of Helmstetter on left-symmetric algebras; for two-step nilpotent $\mathfrak{n}$, by Burde and Dekimpe; and for the complex perfect non-semisimple $\mathfrak{g}$ of dimensions five and six, by Burde and Dekimpe and by Burde, Dekimpe and Monadjem. The proof extends Helmstetter's argument. A post-Lie algebra structure embeds $\mathfrak{g}$ into the holomorph of $\mathfrak{n}$. Conjugations chosen by Whitehead's first lemma along the lower central series of $\mathfrak{n}$ make the translation part of this embedding vanish on a Levi factor of $\mathfrak{g}$, while its determinant stays equal to one, as in Kriebel's treatment of semisimple $\mathfrak{n}$. The proof is formalized in Lean with Mathlib, assuming Levi's theorem and Whitehead's first lemma as stated in Weibel's textbook. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: Combinatorial periods of asymmetric billiard trajectories in the regular pentagon
abstract:
We prove that every even integer other than $2$, $12$, $14$ and $18$ is the combinatorial period, the number of bounces before repeating, of a periodic billiard trajectory in the regular pentagon that does not have five-fold rotational symmetry. Davis and Lelièvre conjectured this in 2018 and checked it up to period $4000$, and Kontorovich and Zhang proved it for almost every even number. As they explain, a theorem of Davis, Fuchs and Tabachnikov turns the question into one about vectors. Each vector $(a+b\varphi,c+d\varphi)$ obtained from $(0,1)$ by products of four explicit $2\times2$ matrices, where $\varphi$ is the golden ratio and $a,b,c,d$ are integers, has the half-period $\ell=a+b+c+d$, and when a congruence modulo $5$ holds it gives such a trajectory of period $n=2\ell$. Varying the power of one of the two triangular matrices in such a product gives half-periods in an arithmetic progression. We give $379$ of these progressions, which together contain every half-period $\ell\ge2$ except nine values. Six of the nine come from explicit trajectories checked in exact arithmetic; the other three are halves of excluded periods. The covering argument is checked in Lean, assuming the cited theorem. Whether the four excluded periods occur is not treated. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: KPP fronts in the 1-1-1 ABC flow speed up linearly in every direction
abstract:
Let $V(x,y,z)=(\sin z+\cos y,\ \sin x+\cos z,\ \sin y+\cos x)$ be the Arnold–Beltrami–Childress (ABC) flow with $A=B=C=1$, and let $c^*_e(K)$ be the minimal speed of pulsating fronts of $T_t+K\,V\cdot\nabla T=\Delta T+f(T)$ in the direction $e$, for a reaction $f$ of KPP type. We prove that $\lim_{K\to\infty}c^*_e(K)/K$ exists and is positive for every unit vector $e$. Zlatoš proved that this limit exists and equals a supremum over first integrals of the flow, and Xin, Yu and Zlatoš, who constructed periodic orbits of this flow, pointed out that a positive-measure tube of orbits moving roughly linearly would make the limit positive, but that a rigorous proof of such tubes was not known. We prove that such a tube exists. Two independent interval-arithmetic computations certify an elliptic periodic orbit with nonzero twist; Pöschel's KAM theorem with frequencies as parameters then gives invariant curves of the return map with a Lipschitz label, which yield a Lipschitz first integral supported on the tube. The deduction from the certified facts is checked in Lean, with Zlatoš's and Pöschel's theorems as cited inputs. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: A four-dimensional 4-reptile simplex
abstract:
A $d$-dimensional simplex is a $k$-reptile if it can be tiled by $k$ mutually congruent simplices similar to it. Matoušek and Safernová conjectured that for $d\ge3$ a $k$-reptile $d$-simplex exists only when $k=m^d$ for an integer $m$, and proved this for $d=3$. Kynčl and Patáková proved that in dimension four $k$ must be a square, noted that every $k$-reptile simplex known in dimension $d\ge3$ has $k=m^d$, and asked whether a four-dimensional $k$-reptile simplex exists with $k$ a square but not a fourth power. We show that the simplex with vertices $(0,0,0,0)$, $(1,0,0,0)$, $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0,0)$, $(\tfrac23,\tfrac13,\tfrac13,0)$ and $(\tfrac34,\tfrac14,\tfrac14,\tfrac14)$, the fundamental alcove of the affine Weyl group of type $F_4$, is a $4$-reptile: it is tiled by four congruent copies of itself scaled by $1/\sqrt2$, two of them mirror images. This answers the question of Kynčl and Patáková with $k=4$ and disproves the conjecture of Matoušek and Safernová in dimension four. The subdivision itself is due to Felikson and Tumarkin, who found in 2004 that the affine reflection group of type $F_4$ has a reflection subgroup of index $4$ whose fundamental simplex is similar to the alcove. What we add is the observation that this settles the reptile question, a short direct proof of the tiling, and exact computer checks of it. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: A lattice parallelepiped with no unimodular triangulation
abstract:
A lattice polytope has a unimodular triangulation if it can be cut into lattice simplices of the smallest possible volume. Haase, Paffenholz, Piechnik and Santos asked in their 2017 survey whether every lattice parallelepiped, and more generally every lattice zonotope, has one. Such polytopes have the integer decomposition property, and Codenotti and Santos proved that every 3-dimensional lattice parallelepiped can be covered by unimodular simplices. We show that the answer is no in every dimension $d\ge 4$. The 4-dimensional parallelepiped $P$ spanned by $e_1,e_2,e_3$ and $(1,2,3,5)$ has no unimodular triangulation, and its products with unit cubes give examples in higher dimensions. Its edges at the origin span a cone that Firla and Ziegler showed cannot be triangulated into unimodular cones generated by its Hilbert basis (its minimal generators). Yet the cone of $P$ at each vertex can be so triangulated with lattice points of $P$: the obstruction is not seen at any vertex. The proof is by hand: points of $P$ with coordinates in $\frac12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\frac14\mathbb{Z}$ force faces into any unimodular triangulation, until one such point lies in none. Checked certificates show that $P$ has a unimodular cover and is, up to lattice equivalence, the unique 4-dimensional example of determinant at most 5. The question in dimension 3 remains open. title: Competitive equilibrium can fail near equal budgets for three additive agents
abstract:
In a Fisher market with indivisible goods, each agent has a budget of artificial money and a competitive equilibrium is an allocation of all the goods with prices at which every agent gets a most preferred bundle within budget. With exactly equal budgets one good and two agents already have no equilibrium. Babaioff, Nisan and Talgam-Cohen proved that two agents with additive preferences over any number of goods have a competitive equilibrium whenever their budgets are sufficiently close to equal but not equal, and asked whether this extends to more than two agents (their Open Problem 1). It does not. We give three agents with strict additive valuations over five goods such that for every $0<\delta<1/17$ no competitive equilibrium exists at the budgets $(1-3\delta,1+2\delta,1+\delta)$, nor at any budget vector near them. So every neighborhood of equal budgets contains a set of positive measure on which no equilibrium exists. Adding goods of small value, as in Segal-Halevi's Lemma 5, extends this to every number of goods $m\ge5$. This answers the case of three additive agents and $m\ge5$ goods that Segal-Halevi left open: the budgets with no competitive equilibrium can have positive measure. The proof gives, for each allocation of the goods, an exact Farkas (linear-programming duality) certificate that no prices support it; an independent exact linear-programming computation confirms it. title: A quadratic lower bound for intervals in the Hales–Jewett theorem
abstract:
A combinatorial line in $[m]^n$ is $q$-fold if its wildcard set, the set of coordinates that vary along the line, is a union of at most $q$ intervals of consecutive coordinates. Let $I(m,r)$ be the least $q$ such that, for $n$ large, every $r$-coloring of $[m]^n$ has a monochromatic $q$-fold line. We show that $I(m,2)>(m-3)^2/128$ for every $m\ge3$, so $I(m,r)\ge I(m,2)$ grows at least quadratically in $m$ for every $r\ge2$. This answers Question 3.1 of Conlon and Kamčev, who asked whether some $m\ge4$, $r\ge2$ and $c>1$ admit $r$-colorings of $[m]^n$ with no monochromatic line whose wildcard set is a union of at most $cr$ intervals: $m=18$, $r=2$ and any $1<c<3/2$ do, for every $n$. For $m=3$ the value is known, $r$ or $r-1$, by work of Conlon and Kamčev, Leader and Räty, and Kamčev and Spiegel; Kamčev and Spiegel noted that $r-1$ is the best explicit lower bound the known methods give, and Shelah's proof of the Hales–Jewett theorem gives the upper bound $\mathrm{HJ}(m-1,r)$. To rule out lines with at most $Q$ intervals, we color $x$ by the parity of $\lfloor S(x)/(32Q)\rfloor$, where $S(x)$ is the sum of the squared differences of consecutive letters of the word $0x$. Along such a line, $S$ is a quadratic in the free letter whose values rise through a whole interval of length $32Q$ in smaller steps, so the line meets both colors. This coloring theorem is proved in Lean from the definitions; the step to $I(m,r)$ is a short argument on paper. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: Connected quandles that refute Hayashi's conjecture
abstract:
We construct connected quandles of orders 1890 and 5670 whose right translations $x\mapsto x*y$ have cycles of lengths 60, 84, 140 and 210. Since 60, 84 and 140 do not divide 210, this disproves the conjecture of Hayashi (2013) that in a finite connected quandle the longest cycle length of a right translation is a multiple of all the others. A quandle is a set with a self-distributive operation modeled on conjugation in a group, and quandles give invariants of knots. The conjecture was known for profiles with at most five cycles (Lages and Lopes), for orders up to 47 (Watanabe) and for affine quandles (Kajiwara and Nakayama). Filipi showed that for conjugation quandles it is equivalent to a group-theoretic conjecture, that a power of an element of a finite generating conjugacy class $C$ is central as soon as it commutes with a suitable element of $C$. Our quandles are conjugacy classes of affine maps, so they refute that conjecture too. The four long cycle lengths are each twice the product of three of the primes 2, 3, 5 and 7, while each right translation has order 420. The construction gives an infinite family, including latin counterexamples (every left translation is also a bijection), and no counterexample from it has order below 1890. The proofs are by hand. Independent programs recompute both quandles, and one checks every quandle axiom on the full operation table. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: Cyclic sieving for q-Kreweras numbers in the exceptional types
abstract:
Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with Coxeter number $h$ and simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. For each $s\ge1$ the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/sh\mathbb{Z}$ acts on the multichains $w_1\le\dots\le w_s$ of noncrossing partitions of $W$. Reiner and Sommers defined, for each nilpotent orbit $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathfrak g$ and each positive integer $m$, a $q$-Kreweras number, a polynomial in $q$, and tabulated it in the exceptional types. Each $W$-orbit of flats $X$ determines a nilpotent orbit $\mathcal{O}_X$, principal in the Levi subalgebra of $X$. Their Conjecture 1.4 says that the $q$-Kreweras number of $\mathcal{O}_X$ with $m=sh+1$, at a primitive $d$-th root of unity, counts the multichains fixed by an element of order $d$ whose bottom element has fixed space in the orbit of $X$. Reiner and Sommers proved it in types $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$. We prove it in types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$, so it holds for every irreducible Weyl group. At $q=1$ the statement is a count proved by Douvropoulos and Josuat-Vergès; what is new is every $d>1$. Krattenthaler and Müller proved the unrefined cyclic sieving, Armstrong's conjecture, in the exceptional types by reducing it to finitely many cases. Using their parametrization of $s$ and of the acting element by three integers, and their description of the fixed points, we show that with two of the integers fixed the fixed-point count is a polynomial of degree at most the rank in the third. A finite-difference argument shows the same for the tabulated $q$-Kreweras number at the root of unity, once it holds for rank plus one consecutive values of the third integer. Only finitely many choices of the fixed pair need a direct check. The resulting finitely many identities are verified by two independent exact programs, and the reduction is checked in Lean. title: The Harborth constant of Cp ⊕ Cp for every prime p ≥ 11
abstract:
The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the least $k$ such that every $k$-element subset of $G$ contains $\exp(G)$ distinct elements whose sum is zero; the exponent $\exp(G)$ is the largest order of an element of $G$. Gao and Thangadurai conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n-1$ for odd $n$, and proved it for primes $p\ge 67$; Gao, Geroldinger and Schmid extended this to $p\ge47$, and Kemnitz had settled $p\in\{3,5,7\}$. Bajnok's Menu of research problems asks for the primes $11\le p\le 43$ (Problem F.100). We prove that $\mathsf g(C_p\oplus C_p)=2p-1$ for every prime $p\ge11$, which answers that problem and, with Kemnitz's values, gives the conjecture for every odd prime. As in the work of Gao and Thangadurai and of Gao, Geroldinger and Schmid, we project the set along a line through $0$, which sorts its points into $p$ parallel lines (fibers), choose a projection in which many pairs of points share a fiber, and use the lifting criterion of Gao and Thangadurai. What is new is a sufficient condition, proved with the theorem of Dias da Silva and Hamidoune, that depends only on how many points each fiber holds and not on where the fibers lie. The analysis of fiber sizes is by hand for $p\ge17$ and a finite check for $p=11$ and $13$. The proof for $p\ge11$ and the lower bound for every odd prime are formalized in Lean. title: Counterexamples to the conjectured characterization of Hamiltonian degree sequences in digraphs
abstract:
We show that the conjecture of Kühn, Osthus and Treglown (2008), proposed as a digraph analogue of Chvátal's theorem, fails for every order $n\ge7$ and holds for $3\le n\le6$. It states that every digraph whose separately sorted out- and in-degree sequences satisfy two Chvátal-type conditions, and a third condition when the order is even, has a Hamilton cycle. It strengthens Nash-Williams' conjecture of 1975, which assumes strong connectivity instead of the third condition. Guninski found 6-vertex counterexamples to Nash-Williams' conjecture on MathOverflow in 2013 and 2020; the 2013 example was confirmed there by Royle and Thomas and the 2020 ones by DeBiasio. All of them violate the third condition. Our counterexamples are an explicit 7-vertex digraph and an explicit family, and the small orders are settled by exhaustive search. Hence Nash-Williams' conjecture fails for every $n\ge7$, in addition to Guninski's case $n=6$, and the same search shows that it holds for $3\le n\le5$. The family also shows that for every $n\ge8$ the conditions of either conjecture do not even force a cycle through every pair of vertices, answering a question recorded by Kühn and Osthus after Bermond and Thomassen. title: A counterexample to the very sparse greedy conjecture for random hitting sets
abstract:
Let $A$ be a random $m\times n$ zero-one matrix with independent Bernoulli$(p)$ entries, whose rows are to be hit by a set of columns. Arpino, Dmitriev and Grometto proved that with high probability the linear programming (LP) relaxation, the fractional hitting set, is within a constant factor of the optimum when $mp\lesssim\log n$, and the greedy algorithm is within a constant factor of the optimum when $p\ge n^{-\delta}$ with $\delta<1/2$. They conjectured that in the very sparse regime $mp\to0$ the ratio of the greedy value to the LP value tends to one. We show that this fails. For $m=k$, $n=k^{10}$ and $p=1/(10k^4)$, with the explicit constant $c=1/(196608\cdot10^9)$, the greedy algorithm that breaks ties by the leftmost column, as in their analysis, uses at least $(1+c/8)$ times the LP value with probability at least $c/4$ for every $k\ge10^{20}$; these parameters satisfy their Assumption 2. The same holds with probability at least $c/8$ when ties are broken uniformly at random. So the ratio does not converge to one in probability. The obstruction is a path of three triples whose middle triple greedy takes first; exchanging it for its two ends saves half a column per path. title: Graceful 4-coloring of planar graphs is NP-complete
abstract:
A graceful $k$-coloring of a graph is a proper vertex coloring with colors $1,\dots,k$ such that, at every vertex, the incident edges receive distinct differences of their endpoint colors. Cyriac Antony, Laavanya D. and Devi Yamini S. proved that deciding graceful $k$-colorability is NP-complete for planar graphs when $k\ge 5$, and for $k=4$ on graphs of maximum degree three, and they left open the complexity of graceful 4-colorability of planar graphs. We prove that this problem is NP-complete, even for planar graphs of maximum degree three (inputs, as in their formulation, may be disconnected). The hardness comes from the reduction of Édouard Bonnet, Dibyayan Chakraborty and Julien Duron, who proved that deciding whether a cubic planar graph has a perfect matching cut (a perfect matching that is exactly the set of edges leaving some vertex set) is NP-hard; we apply their construction to every instance. What we add is an exact correspondence: for every finite cubic graph $H$, the graph obtained by subdividing each edge of $H$ twice has a graceful 4-coloring if and only if $H$ has a perfect matching cut. title: Symmetry of hook+column coefficients in iterated plethysms
abstract:
A hook+column partition $(\alpha,2^\beta,1^\gamma)$ has a first part $\alpha$, followed by $\beta$ parts equal to two and $\gamma$ parts equal to one. Let $g$ be a homogeneous rational symmetric function of degree $d\geq1$, let $a\geq2$, and put $f=g[h_a]$. We prove that, for each fixed $\gamma$, the Schur coefficients of $f$ at these partitions, listed by $\beta$ from $0$ to $d-1-\gamma$, read the same forwards and backwards, zero entries included, and that they vanish for larger $\beta$. Consequently, every iterated plethysm of complete homogeneous functions has symmetric hook+column sequences, answering Question 1 of Gutiérrez and Rosas. They gave explicit formulas for two three-factor families and proved that the second symmetric and exterior plethysms $s_{(2)}[f]$ and $s_{(1,1)}[f]$ of a Schur-positive $f$ preserve flip-symmetry, a stronger form of this symmetry; Langley and Remmel gave the underlying two-factor formula. We extend the symmetry to every number of factors and every positive index, and retain the zero entries. The argument uses Gutiérrez and Rosas's specialization at the signed alphabet $1-x-y$. After division by $(1-x)(1-y)$, replacing $x$ and $y$ by their reciprocals gives the coefficient identity. title: A subdivided 6-clique breaks a conjectured sum bound for independent monophonic-position colorings

title: A proof of Geneson's continuous gluing conjecture
abstract:
Geneson introduced continuous Turán numbers: for a set $R\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ and $n>0$, $\operatorname{opx}(n,R)$ is the supremum of the areas of open subsets of the square $[0,n]^2$ that contain no copy of $R$, where a copy may move the horizontal coordinates of $R$ apart and its vertical coordinates apart, keeping their order, but never closer together. We prove Conjecture 6.3 of Geneson's Continuous Turán numbers: if $P$ and $Q$ share a point $(c,d)$, with $P$ weakly south-west of it and $Q$ weakly north-east of it, then $\operatorname{opx}(n,P\cup Q)\le\operatorname{opx}(n,P)+\operatorname{opx}(n,Q)$ for every $n>0$. The sets $P$ and $Q$ are arbitrary: no finiteness, boundedness or measurability is assumed. Keszegh proved the corresponding inequality for forbidden zero–one matrices joined at opposite corner entries, by partitioning a host matrix according to the possible gluing corners. We carry this partition over to the continuous setting. What we add is compactness of the space of copies in a compact host, which makes the partition measurable, and the inner regularity of Lebesgue measure, which passes from measurable pieces to open sets. title: Faithful local dynamics on every finite acyclic graph
abstract:
Give each vertex of a finite directed acyclic graph a finite set of states, and let updating a vertex overwrite its state with a function of the states at its outgoing neighbors. title: Fathi's consecutive-integers bound does not extend to multitwists
abstract:
On the sphere with five boundary components, a fixed positive multitwist can have exceptional exponents arbitrarily far apart, even when the base map is pseudo-Anosov. More precisely, we give curves $a,c,d$ such that, for every $k\ge1$, the multitwist $t=T_aT_c$ and $g_k=T_a^{-1}T_c^{-(k+1)}T_d$ satisfy Ivanov's filling hypothesis (the component orbits together fill the surface), while $tg_k$ and $t^{k+1}g_k$ fix essential curves. Their exceptional exponents are $k$ apart. Thus Fathi's consecutive-integers bound for a single Dehn twist does not extend to the multitwists in Ivanov's question. Long and Morton proved finiteness of the exceptions for a single twist about an essential curve with a pseudo-Anosov base on a closed orientable surface; on closed surfaces, Fathi confined the exceptional exponents to seven consecutive integers whenever the twisting curve's orbit fills the surface, for any base mapping class. We answer Ivanov's consecutive-integers question for this surface; examples with reducible bases are also given. Penner's construction supplies the pseudo-Anosov bases, and a pants decomposition proves filling. The algebra is verified in Lean and the finite curve and topology calculations by independent exact programs. The weaker question about the number of exceptions remains open.

title: A monotone counterexample to a question on distributional complexity
abstract:
For a Boolean function under a product measure, distributional algorithmic complexity is the minimum expected number of adaptive queries needed to determine its value. Distributional subcube partition complexity is the minimum expected number of fixed coordinates in a monochromatic subcube partition. Köhler-Schindler and Steif asked in 2024 whether these quantities are equal for every monotone Boolean function. We answer their Question 2.1 in the negative with the explicit function $f(x_0,\ldots,x_4)=x_1x_2x_3\lor x_0x_4(x_1\lor x_2\lor x_3)$. For independent fair input bits its algorithmic complexity is $13/4$, while its subcube partition complexity is $51/16$. A finite recurrence proves the algorithmic lower bound, and an explicit partition gives the strict inequality. An exact linear-programming dual certificate proves the partition value is optimal. The strict inequality is formalized in Lean; independent exact checkers verify the additional dual certificate.

title: Locked tromino tilings of rectangles
abstract:
An $m\times n$ rectangle has a locked tromino tiling if and only if $3\mid mn$ and $\min(m,n)\ge4$. A tromino consists of three grid cells connected through shared sides; a tiling is locked if no pair of tiles can be recombined into a different pair and the rectangle has another tiling. We prove the existence direction of Tucker-Foltz's conjecture. Tucker-Foltz showed that rectangles with a side of length at most three have none, constructed locked tilings when one side is divisible by three and at least six and the other is at least one hundred, and conjectured that four suffices. Following Tucker-Foltz's construction by compatible rectangular blocks, we supply the remaining cases and glue them along full rows and columns. Aanjaneya and Pal earlier proved existence on the same rectangles for the different condition of fault-free L-tromino tilings. Lean formalizes the existence theorem for $3\mid m$, $m\ge6$, $n\ge4$, including the gluing argument, arithmetic and finite blocks, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Two separately written programs, sharing no code, check the blocks and seams. The classification uses Tucker-Foltz's preprint theorem for narrow rectangles, whose proof leaves the $m=3$ frontier check to the reader there; we neither repeat nor formalize that check.

title: Existence of locally toroidal regular 4-polytopes
abstract:
We prove the existence half of Schulte–Weiss Problem 16 (2006) and McMullen–Schulte Conjecture 10C7 (2002): the universal regular 4-polytope $\{\{4,4\}_{(s,0)},\{4,4\}_{(u,0)}\}$ exists for every pair of distinct odd integers $s,u\geq3$, with no coprimality assumption. Here $\{4,4\}_{(s,0)}$ is the quotient of the square tessellation by $s\mathbb Z^2$. Finiteness and group classification remain open. The proof constructs four matrices over a finite field of characteristic two whose local subgroups are isomorphic to the prescribed toroidal groups. A commutator obstruction shows that these subgroups meet exactly in the subgroup on their two shared generators; this equality lifts to the universal presentation. The group theorem, the geometric identification of the toroidal maps, and the construction and universality of the resulting abstract polytope are formalized in Lean.

title: Sharp linear bounds for the EKG sequence
abstract:
We prove that the EKG sequence satisfies $13n/28\le a(n)\le12n/7$ for every $n\ge1$, with equality only at $n=28$ and $n=7$, respectively. Discovered by Jonathan Ayres, the sequence starts with $1,2$ and repeatedly takes the least unused positive integer sharing a factor greater than $1$ with its predecessor. This proves the sharp linear bounds conjectured by Lagarias, Rains and Sloane, who established coarse bounds at every index. Hofman and Pilipczuk proved the limits $1/2$, $3/2$ and $1$ of $a(n)/n$ on primes, their triples and the other terms, and Haver made these estimates explicit and formalized them in Lean. Our earlier second-order asymptotic also builds on Haver's work. We sharpen Haver's self-improving early-even bound with a shorter prime window and effective large-sieve constants, and control odd terms so that the analytic range meets a finite computation. title: A counterexample to Stanley's conjecture on Smith forms of Jucys–Murphy elements
abstract:
We disprove Stanley's conjectured Smith-form formula for Jucys–Murphy elements on integral Specht modules: for shape $(3,1,1)$ and $k=3$, the Smith form is $(1,1,1,1,2,2)$ instead of $(1,1,1,1,1,4)$. A second example, of shape $(5,2)$, disproves his conjectural remark that every invariant factor is a product of some of the eigenvalues. For $n\ge3$, we prove in writing that the formula holds at $k=3$ precisely for partitions with at most two rows or at most two columns. The classification holds on every full-rank lattice in the rational Specht module stable under the permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$. Stanley's formula was based on Darij Grinberg's computations. Grinberg also clarified the integral lattice, and Alexander Chervov asked about the conjecture's status. The elements first appeared in Alfred Young's work and were rediscovered by Jucys and Murphy; Vershik and Okounkov give their common eigenbasis and tableau-content eigenvalues. The proof combines those eigenvalues with an integral group-ring identity and explicit integer matrices. Lean verifies the finite matrix calculations and supporting algebraic identities; independent programs identify the matrices with the Specht-module actions outside Lean.

title: Smith normal form of the n-cycle class sum
abstract:
We determine the Smith normal form of multiplication by the sum of all $n$-cycles on the center of $\mathbb{Z} S_n$. For every $n\geq1$, it has $p(n)-n$ zero entries, where $p(n)$ counts partitions of $n$, and nonzero factors $d_0=1$ and $d_r=a_r r!/\gcd(n,r)$ for $1\le r<n$, with $a_r=2$ when $r\equiv n\pmod2$ and $a_r=1$ otherwise. This confirms Stanley's conjectures for odd primes and twice odd primes and gives the $n$-cycle formula for every positive $n$. Goupil and Schaeffer gave a formula for long-cycle connection coefficients, and Biane gave an algebraic proof. We determine the two integral coefficient lattices needed to extract its Smith factors, then prove rowwise divisibility. Grinberg's exposition supplies class-sum and representation-theory background used here. Lean proves the image-lattice statement and divisor chain directly from group-ring definitions, including the character formula. The diagonal form and prime cases follow by written arguments.

title: The three-color Ramsey number of the 10-vertex path
abstract:
We prove $R(P_{10},P_{10},P_{10})=18$: every three-coloring of the edges of $K_{18}$ contains a monochromatic path on ten vertices, and some three-coloring of $K_{17}$ contains none. Faudree and Schelp suggested a formula for three-color path Ramsey numbers. Gyárfás, Ruszinkó, Sárközy and Szemerédi proved that the three-color Ramsey number of the path on $n$ vertices is $2n-2+(n\bmod2)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Dybizbański, Dzido and Radziszowski established the eight- and nine-vertex cases, completing the cases through nine vertices recorded by Radziszowski's survey. The lower-bound coloring is the even-case $K_4$ blow-up given by Gyárfás, Ruszinkó, Sárközy and Szemerédi and by Dybizbański, Dzido and Radziszowski. The new upper bound follows from Boolean satisfiability refutations after fixing a monochromatic nine-vertex path and imposing simultaneous symmetry constraints. A separate refutation proves that the cases considered cover every coloring. The reduction and the certificate checks are formalized in Lean. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. title: Nonexistence of (243,121,60) difference sets in C3 × C9 × C9
abstract:
We prove, by exhaustive computation, that no $(243,121,60)$ difference set exists in $C_3\times C_9\times C_9$. Keita Baba settled this case first on October 4, 2026, by a SAT computation with a certificate accepted by a formally verified checker. We give an independent proof by a different method: a lifting search with the reduction checked in Lean. A difference set with these parameters is a 121-element subset whose ordered differences represent every nonzero group element exactly 60 times. Vera López and García Sánchez recorded this group-specific case as unresolved, and Gordon singled it out in his presentation on the La Jolla Difference Set Repository. The reduction builds on the classical multiplier and character methods of Hall, Menon and Turyn and the multiplier searches of Vera López and García Sánchez. A multiplier-fixed translate has thirteen points in the subgroup of elements annihilated by three. Moment identities, singleton congruences and affine normalizations reduce the problem to eight quotient multiplicity arrays. Complete ternary lifting searches exclude all eight. Lean proves the algebraic reduction, normalization, lifting coverage and pruning lemmas; the final formal nonexistence theorem assumes the search assertions established by the external integer computations.

title: The convex uniform 5-polytopes: a computer-assisted classification
abstract:
We prove completeness of the convex uniform 5-polytope list, conditional on the cited lower-dimensional classifications, the written reductions and the certificate checkers. Its members are Wythoff's constructions of types $A_5$, $B_5$, $D_5$, prisms over uniform 4-polytopes, and products of regular polygons with uniform polyhedra. Conway and Guy announced the four-dimensional classification; Möller gave a complete computer-assisted proof. We extend these neighborhood and radius methods to dimension five. Coxeter's and Johnson's constructions supply the known families. Unbounded polygon sizes require products, forced by neighbor distances and prism cells. title: A planar graph without four- or nine-cycles that is not three-colorable
abstract:
Lu, Wang, Wang, Bu, Montassier and Raspaud asked which cycle lengths, together with length four, force proper three-colorability of planar graphs, as recorded by Kang, Jin and Wang. Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado disproved Steinberg's conjecture for lengths four and five. Kostochka and Yancey proved a sharp general lower bound on the number of edges of a four-critical graph. We give an 82-vertex planar graph without cycles of length four or nine that is four-critical and attains that bound, answering the length-nine case of that question. The graph is obtained by Dirac–Hajós–Gallai–Ore compositions of complete four-vertex graphs. Its non-three-colorability follows by induction on this construction; a rotation system, cycle enumeration and three-colorings after edge deletion establish the remaining properties. Lean verifies the rotation certificate, the exclusion of four- and nine-cycles, and non-three-colorability of the same graph.

title: The second-order asymptotic of the EKG sequence
abstract:
The EKG sequence $a(n)$ starts $1,2$ and thereafter chooses the least unused positive integer not coprime to the preceding term. Jonathan Ayres discovered it, and Lagarias, Rains and Sloane conjectured its additive second-order asymptotic at almost all indices. Haver reduced the asymptotic for the least unused even integer to counting used odd values above it, excluding three times odd primes, and proved the sharp upper bound. Hofman and Pilipczuk proved the weaker ratio limits and prime pattern. Combining these estimates with an elementary sieve and the prime number theorem, we prove the lower bound and transfer to the smoothed sequence. Smoothing $p,3p$ to $2p$ for odd primes gives $b(n)=n+n/(3\log n)+o(n/\log n)$ $(n\to\infty)$, hence the conjectured formula at almost all original indices. We prove Ordowski's nonprime inequality and density-one conjectures, and Jasinski's finiteness conjectures for the three critical lines; we also obtain the below-diagonal asymptotic and finiteness of cycles of each bounded length. Lean formalizes the main theorem.

title: The seventh ternary density Hales–Jewett number
abstract:
Let $c_{n,3}$ be the largest size of a subset of $\{0,1,2\}^n$ containing no combinatorial line, a triple obtained by varying a nonempty set of coordinates through the same letter while fixing the rest.
